To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have defined fully-unintegrated PDFs and FF, and calculated their matching coefficients to standard collinear PDFs and FF.
we have defined, studied, and calculated at one loop the fully-unintegrated PDFs and FF that are relevant for measuring k⊥ in the context of perturbative QCD.
1) We define and calculate at one loop generalized BFs and FJFs, which are fully-un-integrated PDFs and FF for perturbative transverse momenta.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of fully-unintegrated PDFs and FF, which will be useful for future experimental studies of the transverse momentum distributions in the final state of collider processes.

the development of a new framework for the description of fully-unintegrated PDFs and FF in perturbative QCD, which is relevant for the analysis at hadron colliders of a broad class of observables with high sensitivity to the initial-state radiation or to the fragmentation of jets.

the development of new theoretical tools for the description of the collinear radiation in high-energy processes, which are important for the understanding of the structure and the fragmentation of hadrons.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the fully-unintegrated functions can be used to study the collinear radiation from initial- and final-state hadrons in a perturbatively well-defined way, which is a prerequisite for the study of hadronization effects.

generalized BFs and FJFs provide a complete and self-contained description of the perturbative collinear initial and final state of a hadron collider process, and that they are the natural basis for a factorization framework in which transverse momenta are measured.
the present work provides a complete description of fully-unintegrated PDFs and FF at one loop, and that the corresponding BFs and FJFs have been calculated for the first time.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we provide a complete set of ingredients to describe the fully-unintegrated collinear dynamics of QCD processes, which can be used to construct a fully-unintegrated version of the factorization theorem.

, for a large class of semi-inclusive cross sections, we have derived the factorization theorem with fully-unintegrated PDFs and FF, and calculated at one loop the corresponding matching coefficients.
, for the first time, the perturbative parton dynamics in the collinear and soft regions of a hard scattering process are fully described in a unified way.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the fully-unintegrated BFs and FJFs provide a convenient way to describe the transverse-momentum dependence of collinear initial and final states in a way that is manifestly gauge invariant, renormalizable, and free of soft and collinear singularities.
the fully-unintegrated BFs and FJFs are the natural building blocks of factorization theorems for processes where the transverse momenta of the final-state particles are measured.
, for processes involving the full four-momenta of partons, the standard parton distribution and fragmenting functions need to be supplemented by fully-unintegrated BFs and FJFs.
